claims.text: Clinician note records apixaban 5 mg twice daily started on 2026-08-01, with age 84 and weight 58 kg noted.
Creatinine was 140 umol/L on today's sample (2026-08-20).
Age 84 and weight 58 kg are recorded alongside the apixaban start, both below the thresholds mentioned in the dosing reference.

open_questions: Was renal function (creatinine/eGFR) documented before apixaban was started, and what were the prior values? Only a current creatinine of 140 umol/L is recorded.
For how long has apixaban been prescribed, and was the dose ever adjusted for age, weight or renal function? The record shows one start entry only.
Is there a documented indication for apixaban (e.g. atrial fibrillation, VTE), and has bleeding risk been assessed? No indication or bleeding-risk assessment is recorded.
Has the rising creatinine (140 umol/L) been reviewed, and were earlier creatinine values lower? No prior creatinine values appear in the record.
Are there earlier entries recording falls, bleeding or anaemia that would affect anticoagulation safety? None are present in the supplied record.
Were any other anticoagulants or interacting medications discontinued before apixaban started? No such entries are present.
Which allergies or reactions are recorded? No allergy entries appear in the supplied record.
Which follow-ups, referrals or tests are planned or outstanding? No follow-up or monitoring entries appear in the supplied record.
Given age 84, weight 58 kg and creatinine 140 umol/L, does the apixaban 5 mg twice daily dose match the product label's dose-reduction criteria?

citation.quote: Started apixaban 5 mg twice daily. Age 84; weight 58 kg.

candidate_highlights.risk_reason: Age 84, weight 58 kg and creatinine 140 umol/L each meet a criterion in the apixaban label for considering a reduced dose, but the record shows 5 mg twice daily.
candidate_highlights.suggested_action: Ask the prescriber to confirm the apixaban dose against the label's dose-reduction criteria.

candidate_highlights.risk_reason: Creatinine 140 umol/L meets the renal criterion in the apixaban label, and no earlier creatinine values are recorded for comparison.
candidate_highlights.suggested_action: Review the creatinine result with the clinician and confirm whether renal function has been documented previously.

check_points.text: Check whether age 80 or over, weight 60 kg or less, and creatinine 133 umol/L or more have been applied to the apixaban dosing decision.

reference.quote: Reduce the dose to 2.5 mg twice daily when two of the following apply: age 80 or over, weight 60 kg or less, creatinine 133 umol/L or more.

check_points.text: Confirm whether renal function has been checked within the past year for this patient.

reference.quote: Check renal function at least once a year.
